title: Big AI Companies Sued for Agreeing to Slow Down
summary:
Have you ever used an AI chatbot like ChatGPT or Gemini? Some people pay money every month to use them. Now, a new lawsuit says four big AI companies — Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google — made an illegal agreement to slow down their AI development.

The lawsuit was filed on Friday in a court in California. It claims the companies broke antitrust laws. Antitrust laws are rules that stop companies from working together in ways that hurt competition and make prices higher or products worse for customers.

The lawsuit says the deal happened on September 12. That day, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote an essay asking for companies to work together to slow down AI for safety. The same day, OpenAI's Sam Altman, SpaceXAI's Elon Musk, and Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis all agreed publicly.

The people suing are four paid subscribers to ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Gemini. They want to represent all paid subscribers in the U.S. Their lawyer, Nick Rowley, said AI could "spin out of human control and could kill us all" if safety is controlled by private companies.

Amodei had said the government might need to give a special permission for these talks. Altman said OpenAI welcomes a "federal framework" for safety but doesn't need to wait for an antitrust exemption.

The companies haven't responded to the lawsuit yet. The case will go to court.
why_it_matters: Kids already use AI tools for homework, games, and questions, so the rules about who controls AI — and how fast it grows — will shape the world they grow up in.

background_read: Antitrust laws in the United States go back to 1890, when the Sherman Antitrust Act gave the government power to step in when companies blocked competition.

In the late 1990s, the U.S. government took the software company Microsoft to court, saying it broke antitrust rules by tying its web browser to Windows; the case ended with new limits on Microsoft's behavior.

When many people share the same complaint, they can join together in one big case called a class action — that is what these four subscribers are trying to do for everyone in the U.S. who pays for these AI tools.
Elon Musk (a billionaire businessman who runs several companies), Sam Altman (the boss of OpenAI), and Dario Amodei (the boss of Anthropic) are all famous names in the AI world.
Article_Structure: WHO: Four AI companies — Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, and Google — plus four paid subscribers and their lawyer Nick Rowley
WHAT: A lawsuit claiming the companies made an illegal agreement to slow down AI development
WHY: The subscribers say the agreement breaks antitrust laws and could make products worse or cost more for customers

perspectives.description: They say companies should not be allowed to team up and decide together how fast AI grows, because that can push prices up and leave customers with worse choices.
They argue they are talking about safety, not money, and that slowing down is meant to protect people from powerful AI that could get out of control — not to cheat anyone.
They point out that this is a tricky mix: companies working together can be good for safety but still counts as a problem under antitrust law, and courts will have to decide where the line is.
